For we are no better than those who died there." And they wept with a loud voice. Then I answered them and said:
"Take courage, Israel, and do not be sorrowful, you house of Jacob!
For you are remembered before the Most High, and the Mighty One has not forgotten you in the struggle.
For I have not forsaken you nor departed from you, but I have come to this place to pray for the desolation of Zion, and to seek mercy for the humiliation of your sanctuary.
And now go, each one of you to his own house, and I will come to you after these days."
So the people went into the city, as I told them.
And I remained in the field for seven days, as he commanded me, and I ate only of the flowers of the field; plants became my food in those days.
And it came to pass after seven days that I dreamed a dream by night.
And behold, a wind arose from the sea, so that it stirred up all its waves.
And I looked, and behold, that man flew with the clouds of heaven. And wherever he turned his face to look, everything that was seen under him trembled.
And wherever the voice went out from his mouth, all who heard his voice melted, just as it melts upon feeling fire.
And after this I looked, and behold, an innumerable multitude of people was gathered together from the four winds of heaven to wage war against the man who had come up from the sea.
And I looked, and behold, he carved out for himself a great mountain and flew up onto it.
And I sought to see the region or the place from which the mountain had been carved, but I was not able.
And after this I looked, and behold, all who had gathered against him to wage war against him were very terrified, yet they dared to fight.
And behold, as he saw the assault of the oncoming multitude, he did not raise his hand, nor did he hold a spear or any weapon of war; but I only saw

how he sent forth from his mouth something like a stream of fire, and from his lips a breath of flame, and from his tongue he shot forth a storm of sparks. And all these were mingled together—the stream of fire, the breath of flame, and the mass of the storm.

And it fell upon the assault of the multitude that was prepared to fight, and burned them all up, so that suddenly nothing was seen of the innumerable multitude except only the dust of ashes and the smell of smoke. And I looked and was astonished.
And after this I saw the same man coming down from the mountain and calling to himself another multitude, a peaceful one.

And the faces of many people approached him, some of whom were rejoicing and some grieving, while some were in chains and some were bringing those who were to be offered. And from the greatness of my fear I awoke, and I prayed to the Most High and said:
“From the beginning you have shown these wonders to your servant and have considered me worthy to receive my prayer.
And now show me also the interpretation of this dream.
For as I consider in my mind: Woe to those who are left in those days, and much more woe to those who are not left!
For those who are not left will be sorrowful,
understanding what things are laid up in the last days, but not attaining to them. But also for those who are left,
for this reason woe to them! For they will see great perils and many distresses, as these dreams show.
Yet it is easier to incur danger and come into these things than to pass away like a cloud from the world and not see what happens in the last days.” And he answered me and said:
“I will tell you the interpretation of the vision, and I will also explain to you the things of which you have spoken.
Because you spoke of those who are left and of those who are not left, this is the interpretation:
He who brings the danger at that time will himself guard those who fall into danger, who have works and faith toward the Mighty One.
Know therefore that those who are left are more blessed than those who have died.
For this is the interpretation of the vision: As for your seeing a man coming up from the heart of the sea,
he is the one whom the Most High has kept for many ages, who will by himself deliver his creation, and he will direct those who are left.
And as for your seeing go forth from his mouth something like breath and fire and storm,
and that he held neither spear nor weapon of war, yet destroyed the assault of that multitude which had come to fight against him, this is the interpretation:
Behold, the days are coming when the Most High will begin to deliver those who are on the earth.
And bewilderment of mind will come upon those who inhabit the earth.
And they will plan to make war one against another, city against city, place against place, nation against nation, and kingdom against kingdom.
And it will be, when these things happen and the signs occur which I showed you before, then my Son will be revealed, whom you saw as a man ascending.
And it will be, when all the nations hear his voice, each one will leave their own region and the war they have with one another,
and an innumerable multitude will be gathered together into one, as you saw, desiring to come and fight against him.
And he will stand on the top of Mount Zion.
And Zion will come and be made manifest to all, prepared and built, just as you saw the mountain carved out without hands.

And my Son himself will convict the nations that have come of their ungodliness—these things that have drawn near to the storm—and will reproach them to their face with their evil thoughts and the torments with which they are about to be tortured,
which are likened to a flame; and he will destroy them without effort by the Law, which is likened to fire.
And as for your seeing him gather to himself another multitude, a peaceful one,

these are the nine tribes that were taken captive from their own land in the days of King Josiah, whom Shalmaneser the king of the Assyrians led into captivity; and he transported them across the River, and they were taken into another land.
They, however, took counsel among themselves to leave the multitude of the nations and go to a more distant region where the human race had never lived,
so that there at least they might observe their statutes, which they had not kept in their own country.
And they entered through the narrow passages of the Euphrates River.
For the Most High then performed signs for them and stopped the channels of the River until they had crossed over.
For through that region there was a great distance to travel, a journey of a year and a half; indeed, that region is called Arzareth.
Then they lived there until the end of time. And now they have begun to return again,
and the Most High will again stop the channels of the River so that they may cross over. For this reason you saw a multitude gathered in peace,
along with those who are left of your people, who are found within my holy
border. Therefore, when he begins to destroy the multitude of the nations that have gathered together, he will protect the people who remain.
And then he will show them very many portents.”
Then I said, “Sovereign Lord, show this to me: why did I see a man coming up from the heart of the sea?” And he said to me:
“Just as no one can explore or know what is in the depth of the sea, so no one on earth can see my Son or those who are with him, except in the time of his day.
This is the interpretation of the dream which you saw, and why you alone have been enlightened concerning these things.
For you have forsaken your own affairs and devoted yourself to mine, and have searched out my law.
For you have directed your life toward wisdom, and have called understanding your mother.

And on this account I have shown you these things, for there is a reward with the Most High. For after another three days I will speak other things to you and explain to you weighty and wondrous matters.”
Then I set out and went into the field, greatly glorifying and praising the Most High for the wondrous deeds that he performed in their proper time,
and because he governs the times and what is brought about within the times. And I sat there for three days.
And it happened on the third day, as I was sitting under an oak,
behold, a voice came out toward me from a bush and said, “Ezra, Ezra!” And I said, “Here I am, Lord.” And I stood up on my feet. And he said to me:
“I clearly revealed myself in a bush and spoke to Moses when my people were enslaved in Egypt.
And I sent him and led my people out of Egypt, and brought him up to Mount Sinai, and kept him with me for many days;
and I told him many wondrous things, and showed him the secrets of the times and the end of the times. And I commanded him, saying:
‘These words you shall make public, and these you shall hide.’
And now I say to you:
The signs that I have shown, the dreams that you have seen, and the interpretations that you have heard—lay them up in your heart.
For you shall be taken up from among mortals, and henceforth you shall remain with my Son and with those who are like you, until the times are ended.
For the age has lost its youth, and the times are drawing near to old age.
For the age is divided into twelve parts, and ten of them have already passed, as well as half of the tenth part;
so two parts remain beyond the half of the tenth part.
Now therefore, set your house in order, and reprove your people; comfort the lowly among them, and renounce now this corrupt life,
and put away mortal thoughts from yourself, cast off human burdens, strip off now your weak nature, lay aside the thoughts that are most burdensome to you, and hasten to depart from these times.
For evils worse than those which you have now seen happen will take place again.
For in proportion as the world becomes weakened by old age, so much more will evils multiply upon those who inhabit it.
For truth has moved farther away, and falsehood has drawn near. For the eagle which you saw in the vision is already hastening to come.”
And I answered: "I have spoken before you, Lord.
For behold, I will go as you have commanded me, and I will reprove the people who are now present. But who will instruct those who will be born afterward?
For the world is set in darkness, and those who dwell in it are without light,
because your law has been burned; wherefore no one knows the things that have been done by you, or the works that will begin.

If, then, I have found favor before you, send the Holy Spirit into me, and I will write everything that has taken place in the world from the beginning, the things that were written in your law, so that people may be able to find the path, and that those who wish to live in the last times may live."
And he answered me and said: "Go, gather the people, and tell them not to seek you for forty days.
But prepare for yourself many tablets of boxwood, and take with you Sarea, Dabria, Selemia, Ethan, and Asiel, these five who are equipped to write swiftly.
And you shall come here, and I will kindle in your heart a lamp of understanding, which shall not be extinguished until what you begin to write is completed.
And when you have finished, some things you shall make public, and some you shall deliver secretly to the wise. For tomorrow at this hour you shall begin to write."
So I went, as he commanded me, and I gathered all the people and said:
"Hear these words, O Israel:
Our ancestors sojourned at first as foreigners in Egypt, and were delivered from there.
And they received the law of life, which they did not keep, which you also have transgressed after them.
And the land was given to you as an allotment in the land of Zion, yet you and your ancestors committed iniquity and did not keep the ways which the Most High commanded you.
Because he is a just judge, in due time he took away from you what he had given.
And now you are here, and your brothers are farther in the interior than you.
If therefore you will rule over your mind and discipline your heart, you will be kept alive and after death you will obtain mercy.
For judgment will come after death, when we shall live again; and then the names of the righteous will become evident, and the deeds of the ungodly will be shown.
Therefore let no one approach me now, nor seek me for forty days."
So I took the five men, as he commanded me, and we went out into the field and remained there.
And on the next day, behold, a voice called me, saying: "Ezra, open your mouth and drink what I give you to drink."
Then I opened my mouth, and behold, a full cup was offered to me; it was full as if with water, but its color was like fire.
And I took it and drank; and when I had drunk, my heart poured forth understanding, and wisdom increased in my breast, for my spirit retained its memory;
and my mouth was opened, and was not closed any longer.
And the Most High gave understanding to the five men, and they wrote in order what was dictated, using characters that they did not know; and they sat for forty days. They wrote during the day,
and at night they ate bread; but as for me, I spoke by day and was not silent at night.
So in forty days, nine hundred and four books were written.
And when the forty days were completed, the Most High spoke, saying: "Make public the first books that you wrote, and let the worthy and the unworthy read them;
but keep the seventy last ones, so that you may deliver them to the wise among your people.
For in them is the spring of understanding, the fountain of wisdom, and the stream of knowledge." And I did so.
